name: Dural Openframe Boot
description:
A striking mid-calf boot that dispenses with a conventional upper entirely — instead, a series of adjustable alloy straps and polymer rails wrap around the leg in an open cage structure. Originally designed for chrome legs where a closed boot upper would trap heat from servo mechanisms, it has become something of a style statement in Tier 3 circles. The straps are individually adjustable to fit any limb profile, biological or augmented.

It looks industrial and deliberate. On a chrome leg, the cage structure echoes the mechanics beneath. On a biological leg, it's a fashion choice. Either way, people notice.
functionality: Open cage structure accommodates any limb profile including large-format chrome prosthetics. Individual strap adjustment fits variable geometry. Heat-dissipating design for servo-driven limbs.
what_it_says: You're not hiding anything. Your augmentation is part of how you look, and you've built your wardrobe around it.
worn_by: augmented individuals who wear their chrome openly
story_hooks: A specific strap configuration has become a coded signal in certain augmentation communities — worn a particular way, it means you're looking for a specific kind of work.
The rails are strong enough that people have been known to use disassembled Dural boots as improvised restraints or splints.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Ironclad Executive BCI Suite

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal, cage-like boot that exposes the leg while providing structural support through an open framework. The silhouette is architectural and deliberately incomplete—mid-calf height with negative space defining its form. Striking and industrial, it reads as high-tech utility repurposed as statement wear.
physical_description.fit: Adjustable compression via individual straps; accommodates both biological and augmented legs with customizable tension. Not tight, but mechanically snug where the rails contact skin or chrome. The open structure allows airflow and heat dissipation.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer rails with anodized alloy straps (aluminum or titanium alloy). Non-conductive padding at contact points. Treaded composite sole with grip-optimized tread pattern.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, cool polymer with slightly grippy finish on rails. Brushed metal straps with matte anodize. Sole is textured rubber-composite hybrid. Overall tactile quality is engineered and precise.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray polymer rails with darker charcoal anodized alloy straps. Accent stitching in electric blue or neon green on padding. Sole in anthracite with reflective heel strip.
physical_description.closures: 6-8 individual magnetic snap straps running vertically and diagonally across the calf. No laces. Friction-fit heel cup with micro-tension adjustment dial at ankle.
distinctive_features: Open cage framework exposing the leg entirely
Thermal venting ports along the rails
Dural Form branding stamped into heel reinforcement
Modular design—straps can be removed or swapped
Embedded pressure-sensors in contact pads (upper-tier models)
Reflective safety striping on trailing edge
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional-meets-fashion. Accessible to working-class and mid-tier corpo personnel. Not luxury, but deliberately engineered and intentional.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by chrome-augmented workers, cyberware technicians, and street-level operators who've made a virtue of mechanical visibility. Also adopted by Tier 3 fashion-conscious individuals who appreciate industrial aesthetics. Signals practical confidence and augmentation-adjacent style without requiring actual augmentation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually worn broken-in with light scuffing on the rails and micro-scratches from daily contact. Straps show compression marks. Sole exhibits wear patterns matching gait. Padding may show staining from sweat or condensation. Maintained but well-used.
